To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
chronic multitasking has a negative effect on writing performance in a realistic writing scenario.
heavy multitaskers: (1) are worse at switching between tasks, (2) write worse essays in irrelevant conditions, and (3) write better essays in relevant conditions.

Chronic multitaskers are less effective at filtering out irrelevant information than non-chronic multitaskers and, as a result, they perform worse on analytical tasks in the presence of irrelevant information.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how chronic multitasking affects writing quality.
the effects of chronic multitasker habits on analytical writing quality, in a scenario where the writer has access to multiple sources of information, some of them relevant and some of them not.
the effects of chronic multitaskers’ inability to filter irrelevant information on their analytical writing performance.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
chronic multitasking is associated with a general switch cost, but also with an ability to integrate relevant information and an inability to filter irrelevant information.
the effects of multitasking depend on the nature of the tasks, the type of distractor and the level of expertise.
multitasking is bad for writing, and it is bad in a very complex and nuanced manner, which is not yet fully understood.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chronic multitasking is not a single, simple phenomenon.
multitasking is not always a bad thing.
multitaskers have a hard time filtering out irrelevant stimuli and are more likely to get distracted.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of chronic multitaskers on analytical writing depend on whether the distractors are related to the task at hand or not.
multitasking is not a binary trait; rather, it is a spectrum.
chronic multitasking habits are complex and should be studied in realistic scenarios.
